observations: Photo shows a stack of plastic buckets with lids, inside what looks like an unfinished/empty room with bare walls and a window.
Front buckets are labeled 'FINECOAT P.O.P EMULSION PAINT' in red/black packaging, with heavy dried paint residue on the outside and rims.
Other buckets are labeled 'EAGLE PAINTS' in white/green/red packaging, also stained with dried paint.
Lid colors vary (white, yellow, black) suggesting mismatched or replaced lids.
Only a portion of the buckets are visible in the frame; the stack is partly obscured, so an exact count cannot be confirmed from this single photo.

No ruler, tape measure, or size marking is visible to confirm the stated 5L capacity; commercial P.O.P paint/emulsion is typically sold in much larger pails (e.g., 20L), which raises doubt about the stated size.
No interior shots showing cleanliness, cracks, or structural soundness of the buckets.

proof_requests: A full, unobstructed photo of all 21 buckets laid out individually and countable.
A photo with a tape measure or ruler against one bucket to confirm actual volume/size.
Close-up photos of bucket interiors and bases showing no cracks, holes, or heavy residue.
A short video of one bucket being filled with water to check for leaks.
Confirmation of lid fit for each bucket (matching lids closed and sealed).
response.reason: The items are identifiable as used commercial paint pails being resold for water storage, but the claimed quantity, size, and 'slightly used' condition are all unverified or contradicted by the photo, so they must be priced at the worst-case (smaller recoverable count, larger/mismatched size unconfirmed, heavier wear) until better proof is given.
